Legs.Subject: Rational is a valid rational representation before any identity is checked: default(Rational) — whose zero-initialized storage never ran the constructor — reads back as the canonical 0/1 rather than the invalid 0/0, and that reading rounds cleanly to raw zero through FixedPointRounding.TryRoundRational; the constructor refuses an explicit zero Denominator, asserted by exception type AND the parameter name it reports; and the division operator refuses a zero-numerator divisor with DivideByZeroException, for both an explicitly constructed zero and the defaulted one.

Rational reduces on construction — lowest terms, positive denominator, the zero numerator canonical over one — so the record's own equality is rational equality, and the reduction is pinned directly: six operand pairs (6/4, −6/4, 6/−4, 0/3, 2^96/2^40, 7/7) read back their reduced pairs and are fixed points of re-construction, and every operand of the eight-sample battery is in lowest terms. Every field identity below is nonetheless checked by cross-multiplication (a/b = c/d iff a·d = c·b), so the algebra statements do not lean on the reduction they sit beside, over eight operand rationals including a zero numerator, negative numerators and a pair wide enough (2^96 over 2^40) to exercise BigInteger growth.
